lessons.title: Units, compound measures and speed, density and pressure
lessons.summary: Convert between metric units of length, area, volume and mass, and use the compound measures speed, density and pressure, including converting between units such as m/s and km/h.
objectives: I can convert between metric units of length, mass, capacity and time.
I can convert units of area and volume, such as cm² to m² and cm³ to m³.
I can use speed = distance ÷ time, including with times in hours and minutes.
I can use density = mass ÷ volume and pressure = force ÷ area.
I can convert compound units, such as m/s to km/h, and solve multi-step problems.

activities.title: Metric conversions
activities.content:
## The basic facts

| Length | Mass | Capacity |
|---|---|---|
| 10 mm = 1 cm | 1000 mg = 1 g | 1000 ml = 1 litre |
| 100 cm = 1 m | 1000 g = 1 kg | 100 cl = 1 litre |
| 1000 m = 1 km | 1000 kg = 1 tonne | 1 ml = 1 cm³ |

**Rule of thumb:** going to a **smaller** unit means **more** of them, so **multiply**; going to a larger unit, **divide**.

$3.2$ km $= 3.2 \times 1000 = 3200$ m. $450$ g $= 450 \div 1000 = 0.45$ kg.

## Time

60 seconds = 1 minute, 60 minutes = 1 hour, 24 hours = 1 day. Time is **not** decimal: 1.5 hours is 1 hour 30 minutes, and 2 hours 15 minutes is $2\frac{15}{60} = 2.25$ hours.

## Area and volume conversions

This is where mistakes happen. Because $1$ m $= 100$ cm:

- $1$ m² $= 100 \times 100 = 10\,000$ cm²
- $1$ m³ $= 100 \times 100 \times 100 = 1\,000\,000$ cm³

Similarly $1$ cm² $= 100$ mm² and $1$ cm³ $= 1000$ mm³.

So $2.5$ m² $= 25\,000$ cm², and $40\,000$ cm³ $= 0.04$ m³.

Think of a square metre as a square with sides 100 cm: it holds $100 \times 100$ centimetre squares. The conversion factor for area is the length factor **squared**; for volume it is **cubed**.

## Imperial approximations you may be given

5 miles ≈ 8 km, 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 pounds. These are usually stated in the question.

question.text: Match each measurement to its equivalent.
question.hint: Check whether it is a length, area, volume or capacity conversion.

activities.title: Speed
activities.content:
## A compound measure

A **compound measure** combines two units. **Speed** combines distance and time:

$\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$, so $\text{distance} = \text{speed} \times \text{time}$ and $\text{time} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}$.

The unit tells you the calculation: **km/h** means kilometres **divided by** hours. Miles per hour, metres per second work the same way.

**A coach travels 210 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Find its average speed.**

2 h 30 min $= 2.5$ h. Speed $= 210 \div 2.5 = 84$ km/h.

**How long does 126 km take at 84 km/h?**

Time $= 126 \div 84 = 1.5$ h $= 1$ hour 30 minutes.

## Converting time carefully

If a calculation gives 2.35 hours, that is **not** 2 h 35 min. Multiply the decimal part by 60: $0.35 \times 60 = 21$ minutes, so 2 h 21 min.

## Average speed over a whole journey

$\text{average speed} = \dfrac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}$

You cannot just average two speeds. A cyclist going 30 km at 15 km/h (2 hours) and returning at 10 km/h (3 hours) covers 60 km in 5 hours: average speed **12 km/h**, not 12.5.

## Converting m/s to km/h

$1$ m/s $= 3600$ m per hour $= 3.6$ km/h. So multiply by 3.6 to go from m/s to km/h, and divide by 3.6 to go back. 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

question.text: A train travels 264 km in 2 hours 24 minutes. Work out its average speed in km/h.
A sprinter runs at 9.5 m/s. Convert this speed to km/h.
question.hint: Multiply by 3.6, or work out metres per hour first and divide by 1000.

activities.title: Worked example: density
activities.content:
## Mass packed into a volume

$\text{density} = \dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}$

Units are usually **g/cm³** or **kg/m³**. Water has a density of 1 g/cm³ (which is 1000 kg/m³); gold is about 19.3 g/cm³.

**A metal block has volume 40 cm³ and mass 312 g. Find its density.**

$312 \div 40 = 7.8$ g/cm³.

**A cylinder of the same metal has volume 250 cm³. Find its mass.**

$\text{mass} = \text{density} \times \text{volume} = 7.8 \times 250 = 1950$ g $= 1.95$ kg.

**A piece of oak has density 0.75 g/cm³ and mass 600 g. Find its volume.**

$\text{volume} = \text{mass} \div \text{density} = 600 \div 0.75 = 800$ cm³.

## Density of a mixture

To find the density of two substances combined, add the **masses** and add the **volumes**, then divide. Never average the two densities.

*100 cm³ of liquid A (density 1.2 g/cm³) is mixed with 300 cm³ of liquid B (density 0.8 g/cm³).*

Mass of A $= 120$ g; mass of B $= 240$ g. Total mass 360 g; total volume 400 cm³.

Density of mixture $= 360 \div 400 = 0.9$ g/cm³.

## Matching units

If density is in g/cm³, the volume must be in cm³ and the mass in g. Convert first if the question gives litres or kilograms.

question.text: A solid cuboid measures 5 cm by 4 cm by 10 cm and has a mass of 1.7 kg. Work out its density in g/cm³.
question.hint: Volume $= 5 \times 4 \times 10$ cm³. Convert the mass to grams.
question.explanation: Volume $= 200$ cm³. Mass $= 1700$ g. Density $= 1700 \div 200 = 8.5$ g/cm³.

activities.title: Pressure and the formula triangles
activities.content:
## Pressure

$\text{pressure} = \dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}$

Force is measured in **newtons (N)**, area in m² or cm², so pressure is in **N/m²** (also called pascals) or N/cm².

**A box weighing 480 N rests on a base of area 0.6 m². Find the pressure on the floor.**

$480 \div 0.6 = 800$ N/m².

The same box standing on a smaller end of area 0.2 m² exerts $480 \div 0.2 = 2400$ N/m²: a smaller area means greater pressure. That is why sharp knives cut and snowshoes stop you sinking.

**A pressure of 50 N/cm² is applied over 12 cm². Find the force.**

$\text{force} = \text{pressure} \times \text{area} = 50 \times 12 = 600$ N.

## The three formulas together

| Measure | Formula | Typical units |
|---|---|---|
| speed | distance ÷ time | m/s, km/h, mph |
| density | mass ÷ volume | g/cm³, kg/m³ |
| pressure | force ÷ area | N/m², N/cm² |

Each has the same shape: one quantity divided by another. To rearrange, remember: the top of the fraction equals the measure times the bottom. The unit of the measure always tells you which is which: *per* means *divided by*.

## Other compound measures

Rates such as **litres per minute**, **price per kilogram** or **people per km²** (population density) all work exactly the same way.

question.text: A force of 900 N acts on an area of 1.5 m². Work out the pressure in N/m².
A time calculation gives an answer of 3.4 hours. What is this in hours and minutes?

options.feedback: 0.4 of an hour is not 40 minutes; hours are not decimal.

activities.title: Common mistakes
activities.content:
## Watch out for

- **Area and volume conversions.** 1 m² is 10 000 cm², not 100. 1 m³ is 1 000 000 cm³.
- **Decimal time.** 1.25 hours is 1 h 15 min. Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60 *before* calculating speed.
- **Mixed units.** If speed is in km/h, distance must be in km and time in hours. Convert before you divide.
- **Averaging speeds.** Use total distance ÷ total time.
- **Averaging densities.** Add masses and volumes separately.
- **Rounding too early**, especially with time in hours as a recurring decimal such as 0.333...
- **Units in the answer.** A number without a unit can lose a mark. Write km/h, g/cm³ or N/m² as appropriate.
- **Which way to rearrange.** Check with the units: g/cm³ = grams ÷ cm³, so mass = density × volume.

question.text:
A metal bar is a cuboid measuring 2 cm by 3 cm by 25 cm. The metal has a density of 8.9 g/cm³.

(a) Work out the mass of the bar in kilograms.

(b) The bar stands upright on its 2 cm by 3 cm end. Its weight is 13.4 N. Work out the pressure it exerts on the surface, in N/cm².

(c) The bar is transported 150 km at an average speed of 60 km/h. How long does the journey take? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
question.hint: (a) Volume first, then mass = density × volume, then convert to kg. (b) Force ÷ area with area = 2 × 3. (c) Time = distance ÷ speed, then convert the decimal.
question.explanation: (a) Volume $= 150$ cm³; mass $= 8.9 \times 150 = 1335$ g $= 1.335$ kg. (b) Area $= 6$ cm²; pressure $= 13.4 \div 6 = 2.23$ N/cm² (3 s.f.). (c) $150 \div 60 = 2.5$ h $= 2$ hours 30 minutes.

activities.title: Key points
activities.content:
- Length: × or ÷ by 10, 100, 1000. **Area**: square the factor (1 m² = 10 000 cm²). **Volume**: cube it (1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³).
- Time is not decimal: convert minutes to hours by ÷ 60, and decimal hours to minutes by × 60.
- **Speed** = distance ÷ time; **density** = mass ÷ volume; **pressure** = force ÷ area. The unit tells you the formula ("per" means divide).
- Average speed uses total distance ÷ total time; mixture density uses total mass ÷ total volume.
- m/s to km/h: × 3.6.
- Match units before calculating and give units with every answer.

practiceQuestions.hint: How many centimetre squares fit along each side of a metre square?
practiceQuestions.explanation: False. A square metre is 100 cm by 100 cm, so it contains $100 \times 100 = 10\,000$ cm².

practiceQuestions.text: A cyclist rides for 1 hour 45 minutes at an average speed of 16 km/h. How far does she travel, in km?
practiceQuestions.hint: 1 h 45 min = 1.75 h. Distance = speed × time.

practiceQuestions.text: A car travels 63 miles at an average speed of 42 mph. How many minutes does the journey take?
practiceQuestions.hint: Time in hours = 63 ÷ 42, then convert to minutes.

practiceQuestions.text: A stone has a mass of 156 g and a volume of 60 cm³. Work out its density in g/cm³.
Silver has a density of 10.5 g/cm³. Work out the volume of a silver ring with mass 4.2 g, in cm³.
A pressure of 250 N/m² is exerted by a force of 75 N. Work out the area in m².
Put these speeds in order from slowest to fastest.
practiceQuestions.hint: Convert everything to the same unit: m/s × 3.6 = km/h; 5 miles ≈ 8 km.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 10 m/s = 36 km/h; 25 mph ≈ 40 km/h; 45 km/h; 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

practiceQuestions.text: Jo drives 60 km at 30 km/h and then 60 km at 60 km/h. She says her average speed is 45 km/h. Explain why Jo is wrong and give the correct average speed.
practiceQuestions.hint: Work out the time for each part.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The first part takes 2 hours and the second takes 1 hour: 120 km in 3 hours. Average speed $= 120 \div 3 = 40$ km/h. You cannot average the speeds because she spent longer at the slower speed.

markScheme.criterion: Explains that average speed is total distance ÷ total time (or that more time is spent at the slower speed), so speeds cannot simply be averaged

practiceQuestions.text:
200 cm³ of liquid X with density 1.1 g/cm³ is mixed with 300 cm³ of liquid Y with density 0.9 g/cm³.

Work out the density of the mixture. Give your answer in g/cm³.
practiceQuestions.hint: Find the mass of each liquid, add the masses, add the volumes, then divide.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Mass of X $= 220$ g; mass of Y $= 270$ g. Total mass 490 g; total volume 500 cm³. Density $= 490 \div 500 = 0.98$ g/cm³.

markScheme.criterion: Total mass 490 g and total volume 500 cm³
